binders: For every pair of real-valued functions a, factor : Fin n -> R, equivalently two real vectors (a_i) and (factor_i) of common length n.
hypotheses: The exact finite sum S = sum_{i in Fin n} a_i is nonzero.
For every index i in Fin n, |factor_i - 1| <= gamma.
conclusions: Let T = sum_{i in Fin n} a_i factor_i and K = (sum_{i in Fin n} |a_i|)/|S|. Then |T-S|/|S| <= gamma K.
mathematical_definitions: The index set Fin n consists of the n positions 0,...,n-1, and every displayed sum is over all of these positions.
S = sum_{i in Fin n} a_i.
T = sum_{i in Fin n} a_i factor_i.
K = (sum_{i in Fin n} |a_i|)/|sum_{i in Fin n} a_i|.
All operations are exact real operations, and |x| is the standard scalar real absolute value max(x,-x).
The only explicit constants are the real numbers 0 and 1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any dimension n, any real vectors a and factor of length n, and any real gamma, assume that the sum of the entries of a is nonzero and that every factor differs from one in absolute value by at most gamma. Then the absolute difference between the weighted sum sum_i a_i factor_i and the original sum sum_i a_i, divided by the absolute value of the original sum, is at most gamma times the ratio of sum_i |a_i| to the absolute value of sum_i a_i.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: No positivity or nonnegativity assumption is stated for the entries a_i or factor_i.

No explicit assumption gamma >= 0 is stated. If all hypotheses are satisfiable, then n cannot be zero and the pointwise absolute-value bound forces gamma >= 0; for gamma < 0 the implication is vacuous.
No explicit assumption n > 0 is stated. When n = 0, S is the empty sum 0, so the hypothesis S != 0 is false and the proposition is vacuous.
If sum_i a_i = 0, the proposition makes no claim because its nonzero-sum hypothesis fails.
The nonzero-sum hypothesis ensures that |S| is nonzero, although real division itself is a total Lean operation.
The only norm-like operation on individual scalars is real absolute value; sum_i |a_i| is the finite l1 sum of the entries of a.

The proposition contains no floating-point format, rounding operation, computed approximation, probabilistic assumption, or finite-precision error model; all quantities and sums are exact real quantities.

There are no existential quantifiers, witness dependencies, or conjunction-valued conclusions. All data are universally quantified, the two assumptions are implications' premises, and the conclusion is one inequality.
No upper bound such as gamma < 1, no sharpness statement, and no equality characterization is encoded.
